items.text: fixed: the MIDI tab in the heads-up display's footer has its icon again (it had none, because the MIDI button it was copied from is built later than the tabs).

changed: the Statistics pane is two columns on a wide screen: the reading, the sounding/muted/empty bar and the column and row bars on the left, the colour-by-shape circles filling the right, so it fits on one page on an iPad in landscape. On a narrow screen it stacks.

changed: Halo and drawing no longer jump between each other. In Edit the colour and mark bar stays in place, dimmed and still while Halo is on, and lights up when you draw, so nothing slides, overlaps or resizes the stage.

fixed: while drawing, tapping Colour or Shape no longer switches itself on and off with nothing happening; any of them (or Halo) takes you back to Halo. Colour and Shape still start drawing from Halo.
Settings has a Size row (Small, Medium, Large). It scales the buttons of the bar and the rails (Medium is the size they have always been), and is kept on this device.

a Statistics pane in the heads-up display (its last tab). It counts the score and says what the numbers show: which colour leads and how evenly the colours are shared, how much is struck, held or gliding, and how much of the grid is silent (empty cells and marks under muted lines). A field of circles shows every colour against every shape (solid = sounding, dashed ring = also counting muted lines), with bars for sounding, muted and empty, and for the marks in each column and row. It follows the score while you look.
fixed: "copy report" in the self-test card now turns green with a tick and says Copied for a moment, so you can see it worked.

fixed: in Edit with Halo off, the colour and mark bar no longer pushes the bottom bar off the screen and makes the page scroll. The stage now makes room for the bar when it appears (and takes the room back when it goes), counting its margins and gap.

changed: switching Halo on and off in Edit now morphs: the colour and mark bar slides up and grows its room (and slides down and gives it back), instead of snapping. The pencil's other changes (Performance, view, MIDI leaving the right rail) slide the same way.
changed: in Edit, the heads-up display button stays at the bottom of the right rail, where it is in play, so it is where your hand looks for it.

changed: in Edit, on an iPad or desktop the colours and the eight mark types now sit together on one compact centred line (smaller, close-set buttons) instead of spreading across the whole width. Phones keep the two-row layout.
